caption.text: TypeScript's union types are useless until you can prove which member you're holding — and `as` is a lie, not a proof. This field guide walks every guard the compiler actually understands: typeof and its null trap, instanceof and its cross-realm failures, discriminated unions, your own predicates and asserts signatures, and never for compile-time exhaustiveness. 10 pages of dense notes, including the places where narrowing silently breaks and a closing cheat sheet.
